attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. Not a quote of Yudkowsky, Bostrom or Englander.

semantics.note: Faithful. The firm part is an evaluative observation: no solid argument shows p(doom) is zero or infinitesimal. The hedged concession about weak arguments is kept as context and correctly left unscored.

contract.note: Reading 'solid' as justified premises covering overall risk is fair and ordinary. Still, 'solid' and 'infinitesimal' have no fixed threshold, so the result depends on evaluator judgment. The contract rightly flags this.

evidence.note: The XPT preprint was available before the post. It shows persistent expert disagreement on AI extinction risk. Disagreement does not show whether any negligible-risk argument is sound.

A dated skeptical argument from May 2023. It challenges one mechanism (fanatical maximisers), relies on assumptions it does not defend, and admits catastrophe routes remain. It does not establish negligible overall risk, so it does not contradict.

reviews.rationale: Neither item meets the support or contradiction condition. e2 attacks one mechanism, not total risk. e1 shows only that experts disagree. No comprehensive evaluation of negligible-risk arguments is in the packet, so the universal negative cannot be confirmed or refuted from this evidence.
